block-in-cat.summary: Block in the curled cat as one flat Mid gray shape lying in the blanket.
block-in-cat.tip: The sleeping tabby cat is about 15 in wide and 7 1/4 in tall: its top is about 1 1/4 in from the top edge, its left side about 1 in from the left edge, and its right side at the right edge. Give it the two pointed ears and the long, low curve of the back where the after picture has them. Its bottom tucks into the yellow knit blanket, so leave the blanket's front roll showing below the sleeping tabby cat.

lines.6: Start with the big oval of the body. Then add the round head and its two pointed ears, and the curve of the back, in curved pieces like ( ), as the after picture shows.
lines.7: It should leave one solid gray shape, its pieces joined with no gaps, as in the after picture.

shade-cat.summary: Paint Dark gray over the cat, leaving the first gray only where white patches go.
shade-cat.tip: The after picture puts Dark gray over almost all of the sleeping tabby cat, not only inside the outlined area: leave the first gray showing only for the muzzle, the two front paws and the patch on its side, where the after picture has them. Pull a darker curved line where the head meets the body and along the tail wrapped in front of the body. Bend the strokes over the back, from the top of each curve down, and keep them off the blue wall.

paint-white-patches.summary: Paint the white muzzle, the two front paws and the white patch on the cat's side.
paint-white-patches.tip: Fill the lighter gray spots step 14 left: the biggest mark (the muzzle and the two paws) is about 3 1/2 in wide, its left side about 3 1/4 in from the left edge, and the patch on its side has its middle about 9 1/4 in from the left edge. Paint the muzzle first, then the paws, leaving a thin gray line between the two paws and between the toes, as the after picture shows. Pull the side patch along the curve of the body with ragged, feathery ends so it melts into what step 14 painted.
